title: The base-changed affine ind-etale basis is dense
statement: For a universal homeomorphism r:X→Y with Y affine, the composite Y.AffineProEt → Y.ProEt → X.ProEt exhibits the affine ind-etale topology of Y as a dense subsite of the pro-etale topology of X.

proof.text: The equivalence of affine ind-etale categories and the dense inclusion of X.AffineProEt imply cover-density of their composite. Both are fully faithful, so local fullness and faithfulness follow.

A covering sieve on an affine basis object contains a finite jointly surjective family. Express the arrows of such a family in the pushforward sieve as composites of basis pullbacks with arbitrary arrows. Surjectivity of the base-change projections then descends joint surjectivity to the original basis arrows, giving a covering family contained in the original sieve. Conversely, base change and the dense inclusion preserve coverings. Finite jointly surjective basis families cover because the arrows are weakly etale, the sources and target are affine, and the family is finite, hence a quasi-compact cover.

theorem proEtaleAffineBaseChange_isDenseSubsite {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Y]
    (r : X ⟶ Y) [IsUniversalHomeomorphism r] :
    (AffineProEt.toProEt Y ⋙ proEtaleBaseChange r).IsDenseSubsite
      (AffineProEt.topology Y) (ProEt.topology X)
